thesis_at_purchase_vs_now: Original thesis: bought as a price-to-value gap; value gap now closed [D04], [D07].
Earnings record: record profit growth observed through 2006, but the commodity environment is now very different from the original purchase period [D02].
Capital allocation: OCF less capex has declined significantly, indicating rising replacement investment costs [D06].
final.price_vs_value_now: The stock trades at approximately 14.53x P/E with a 3.11% dividend yield, which represents a full valuation relative to integrated oil peers [D04], [D06].
final.after_tax_hurdle: Selling will trigger a 35% federal tax cost on the substantial capital gain; however, given the closure of the price-to-value gap and the availability of better long-term alternatives, the sale clears the hurdle [D04], [D08].

drivers.driver: The original thesis was a price-to-value gap, and the market value has now caught up to our appraisal of intrinsic value [D04], [D07].
Operating cash flow net of capital expenditures has fallen 37.6% despite rising net income, signaling increased capital intensity and lower owner earnings [D06].
The valuation multiples (14.5x P/E) are now consistent with, or exceed, those of integrated majors in a cyclical commodity sector [D04], [D06].

final.memo:
When we purchased our stake in PetroChina in 2002–03, we were buying a business at an attractive price-to-value gap [D07]. That gap has now closed; the market value has caught up with our appraisal of intrinsic value [D04]. As a commodity producer, we do not view this as a permanent franchise to be held regardless of price [D04].

While the company has reported record profits [D02], the underlying economics have shifted. Capital expenditures have risen sharply while cash generation net of those investments has declined [D06]. We must also recognize that a record annual result in a commodity business is not a guaranteed perpetual annuity [D03].

We are not in the business of holding commodity producers when the price no longer offers a margin of safety [D04]. Although selling incurs a 35% tax cost, the capital is better deployed elsewhere [D08]. We are liquidating our position to reallocate funds toward more compelling opportunities [D08].
